sections.h2: Where is the Rockingham County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Find it at 170 NC Hwy 65, Suite 150, Reidsville, NC 27320, phone 336-342-8820, fax 336-342-6209. The office is open on weekdays, and its recording policy takes documents until the 4:30 cutoff on days the county is open.

Staff describe the office as a recording agency. They do not draft documents, fill in forms or search title, so a Rockingham County seller normally relies on a closing attorney to prepare the deed and carry it to the counter. The county's own advice on legal forms is to consult an attorney.

sections.h2: What does a deed need before the Rockingham County office will record it?
sections.html:
The office publishes a checklist, and a deed that skips an item can be turned away or hit with an added fee. These are the points that most often matter for a house sale:

  • The first page names the person or law firm that drafted the deed, since North Carolina-prepared deeds and deeds of trust must show it.
  • The grantee's mailing address is printed on the face of the deed so the tax office knows where to send the bill.
  • A notarized paper carries an acknowledgment with the notary's seal and the commission expiration date.
  • The amount of the excise stamp is written on the face of the conveyance, or the letters NTC (no taxable consideration) appear when none is owed.
  • Nobody puts a Social Security, bank, card or license number into the document. The rule allows only the last four digits if an identifier must appear.
  • Mailed items come with a check or money order payable to the Rockingham County Register of Deeds and a stamped return envelope. Returned checks cost $25.

None of this needs to be solved alone on closing day. It matters most for a family deed, a deed into a trust, or a sale where no attorney is involved.

sections.h2: What formatting rules does Rockingham County enforce?
sections.html:
The office applies the statewide standard in G.S. 161-14 and adds a $25 non-standard fee on top of the recording fee when a document misses it. Its printed standards call for letter or legal paper and black type on white, with a blank three-inch band at the top of page one and quarter-inch margins around the rest.

The first page also has to name the type of instrument below that band. Type must be at least nine points and sit on one side of the sheet. Pen is acceptable for filling blanks and making corrections, ideally in black ink. Satisfactions, cancellations and military discharges are exempt, as are separately recorded plats under G.S. 47-30. The register may excuse a slightly small font if the print copies cleanly, but the county advises staying above nine points.

sections.h2: Which fees does the Rockingham County office list?
sections.html:
The county posts a full schedule that mirrors the state fee statute. The lines below matter most to someone selling a house, in the county's wording.

Selected Rockingham County Register of Deeds fees as posted on the county fee schedule
ServicePosted fee
Instruments in general (not deeds of trust)$26.00 for the first 15 pages, $4.00 each added page
Deeds of trust and mortgages$64.00 for the first 35 pages, $4.00 each added page or fraction
Multiple instruments in one document$10.00 for each added instrument
Excess recording data$2.00 for each party listed beyond 20
SatisfactionsNo fee
State excise tax on real estate conveyances$2.00 per thousand ($1.00 up to $500.00)
Certified copy of land records$5.00 for the first page, $2.00 each added page
Uncertified copy$0.25 per page
Notarial act$10.00 per principal signature

The schedule also lists passport, marriage license and vital record fees, which have nothing to do with a sale. The county page notes that an uncertified plat copy at 18 by 24 inches or larger costs $3.00 a page.

sections.h2: How is the excise tax figured on a Rockingham County deed?
sections.html:
The seller pays $1 for each $500 of price, with any leftover amount counted as a full $500. The county's checklist gives two examples. A price of $27,900 rounds up to $28,000 and produces $56 of tax. A price of $32,200 rounds up to $32,500 and produces $65.

The grantor reports and pays it to the register before the deed can be accepted. Write NTC on the face if no tax is due. Half of the revenue stays with the county general fund and the rest is sent to the state, which is why the tax shows up as a line on the seller's side of the closing statement.

sections.h2: How are Rockingham County recordings processed, and when is the cutoff?
sections.html:
The office processes in-person filings first, then e-recordings, then priority mail such as UPS or FedEx, then regular mail. Each item has to be opened, reviewed and found acceptable before it is recorded.

The 4:30 p.m. cutoff applies to paper and electronic filings alike. A person standing in line at 4:30 is served that day, and anyone arriving later waits until the next business day. When the recording date carries real weight, the county's advice is to deliver the instrument in person and wait until it is recorded.

E-recording is accepted during business hours. The county lists three benefits: the recorded document comes back right away, nobody has to travel, and a rejection is flagged immediately. Ask the office for its list of approved e-recording vendors.

sections.h2: How do I look up Rockingham County land records and mortgage releases?
sections.html:
The E-Vault is the county's public search site for land records. The county explains that for 1789 through 1995 the official index is the paper index inside the office, with scanned copies under an Old Index Books tab, and that from 1996 on the electronic database in the office is the official index. Vital records are not in the E-Vault, and the county says its website records are unofficial, so the office holds the official set.

Fresh filings appear first in a temporary index shown in red entries and move to the permanent index, in blue, after full indexing. Use fewer characters in the search fields for better results.

For mortgage releases, the lender holds the duty of filing a satisfaction when a loan is paid off. Recording a satisfaction is free, and the county says to reference only one original instrument per satisfaction to avoid a $25 charge for each extra reference. A payoff does not create a new deed. A copy of the satisfaction can be pulled from the E-Vault or at the office.

sections.h2: What should a Rockingham County seller confirm before closing?
sections.html:
Confirm that every old loan shows a recorded satisfaction and that the vesting deed matches the name on the contract. A missing release is the most common snag, and a buyer's title insurer will ask for it.

  • Search the E-Vault for the last deed and any deed of trust on the parcel.
  • Ask the lender about any loan paid off years ago with no release showing.
  • Confirm that the grantee's mailing address and the drafter's name are on the deed.
  • Ask the attorney whether the deed goes by e-recording or in person at Reidsville.

Under North Carolina law a deed carries no weight against later buyers or lien creditors until it is on the record of the county holding the parcel, and rank follows registration time. That is why buyers push for same-day recording after funds move.

faqs.q: What are the Rockingham County Register of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: The office is open Monday through Friday during business hours, and recording stops at 4:30 p.m. Arrive before that cutoff to have a deed recorded the same day.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to record a mortgage satisfaction in Rockingham County?
faqs.a: No, recording a satisfaction is free. The county charges $25 for each extra reference when one satisfaction document points to more than one original instrument, so list only one.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed by mail in Rockingham County?
faqs.a: Yes. Mail the original with a check or money order made out to the Rockingham County Register of Deeds and a stamped return envelope. Do not mail cash. Mail is processed after in-person, electronic and priority-mail filings.

faqs.q: How is the deed excise tax calculated in Rockingham County?
faqs.a: The seller pays $1 per $500 of price, rounding up to the next $500. The county's example turns a $27,900 price into $28,000 and a $56 tax.

faqs.q: Does the Rockingham County register of deeds search title for me?
faqs.a: No. The office says it is a recording agency and cannot help complete forms or run a title search. Hire an attorney or title agent for that, and use the E-Vault for your own look at the record.
